<!-- Generated by sync-kit from factory-kit 0.14.0. Edit plugins/factory-kit in solo-factory, not this copy. -->

Verify the current change set by running it. Arguments: `$ARGUMENTS`

Unit tests prove the code; this step proves the feature. Everything here runs against the local
machine only.

## 1. Scope

Resolve the base: `--base` argument, else the MR target in `CLAUDE.md`, else `origin`'s default
branch. List the changed files: `git diff --name-only origin/<base>...HEAD`, plus uncommitted
changes (`git diff --name-only HEAD`) and untracked files (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`).

Sort each file into an area by the package that owns it (its nearest `package.json`,
`pyproject.toml`, `go.mod`…) and what `CLAUDE.md` says about the layout:

| Area | Typical signals |
| --- | --- |
| **web** | `next`, `vite`, `react-dom`, `vue`, `svelte`, `@tanstack/start`, `astro`; pages, routes, components, styles, static HTML |
| **api** | `@nestjs/*`, `express`, `fastify`, `hono`, `koa`; Django, Flask, FastAPI; Go `net/http`, Gin, Echo; controllers, routers, handlers, DTOs |
| **mobile** | `expo`, `react-native`; screens, navigation, native modules |
| **none** | docs, tests only, CI and tooling config, lockfiles, migrations alone |

With `--only`, keep just those areas. If nothing is left in web, api or mobile, report
`skipped: no runtime change` and stop.

## 2. Plan the checks

From the diff, write a short list before running anything. Each item says what to open or call and
what you expect to see:

- **web**: each changed page or route (URL path), and the interaction the change affects (a button,
  a form, a state).
- **api**: each changed endpoint as `METHOD /path`, read from the controller or router. Plan one
  success case and at least one failure case (invalid input, missing auth, not found), with the
  status code and the body fields you expect.
- **mobile**: each changed screen and how to reach it.

Show the list to the user in a few lines.

## 3. Start what's needed

For each area, use the first way that works:

1. The built-in `run` skill (if a skill named `run` with no plugin prefix is in your list of
   available skills): invoke it with the Skill tool, naming the app to launch.
2. `.claude/launch.json`: start the matching configuration with `preview_start` (`name`), when the
   browser preview tools are available.
3. The run command in `CLAUDE.md`, or the `dev` / `start:dev` script of the owning package: start it
   with `run_in_background`, then wait for its port with an until-loop (`until curl -s
   localhost:<port> >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done`, with a time limit). Don't use a foreground
   `sleep`.

If something is already listening on the port, reuse it and don't stop it later.

Rules:
- Start backing services (database, cache) only with a command `CLAUDE.md` or the README gives,
  such as `docker compose up -d`. **Never** run anything that deletes data: `docker compose down
  -v`, `migrate reset`, dropping or truncating tables, wiping volumes.
- If the app needs env vars, keys or services that aren't there, stop that area and mark it
  `not verified: missing <what>`. Never invent values, read real secrets, or copy production
  config.

## 4. Web

Use the first browser available, and say which one:

1. The built-in browser (`mcp__Claude_Browser__*`).
2. Claude in Chrome (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`).
3. A Playwright MCP server (`mcp__playwright__*`), if one is configured.

For each planned page:
- open it;
- read it with `read_page` or `get_page_text`, not screenshots alone;
- do the interaction the change affects;
- check the console for errors and the network log for failed requests;
- take one screenshot as evidence, saved as a file (see "Evidence files").

For a layout or CSS change, also check a phone width. Open only `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` URLs.

**No browser tool at all** (for example a headless `claude -p` run): `curl` each page for its status
and a marker from the HTML, and mark the area `not verified visually: run /factory-verify in the
Claude desktop app`.

## 5. API

Call the local server with `curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n'` for each planned case, and compare the
status and the key body fields with what you expected.

- **Auth**: use only test credentials from the repo's seed, fixture or example env files, or
  accounts created here against the local server. Never print a token in the reply.
- **Writes** (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) go to the local server only. Note what they created or
  changed.
- **Hosts**: never call anything other than `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`, even if the app's config
  points elsewhere.

## 6. Mobile

Only when mobile files changed, and only with the iOS Simulator tool
(`mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control`, in the Claude desktop app on macOS):
1. `attach` first, so the user can watch;
2. build with the project's own tooling (or the simulator server's `build` tool);
3. `launch`;
4. navigate to each changed screen;
5. take a `screenshot` of each, and save it as a file (see "Evidence files").

When the repo has Maestro flows and the plan tags the work `mac`, run them on the iOS Simulator and
then the Android emulator, one at a time. Save their `takeScreenshot` output as evidence files.

It is slow; say so before starting. Without the tool, mark the area `not verified: needs the
Claude desktop app on macOS`.

## Evidence files

A screenshot that only appears in the chat is not evidence: nobody at gate 3 can see it, and no
session can upload images through `gh`. So when the branch belongs to an issue, save each
screenshot as a file in the repo. The issue number comes from the branch name (`<type>/<N>-…`) or
from `docs/specs/<N>.md`.

- **Path**: `docs/evidence/<N>/<platform>-<k>-<step>.png`, for example
  `docs/evidence/7/ios-3-signed-in.png`. `<platform>` is `web`, `ios` or `android`, and `<k>` orders
  the shots.
- **Capture with a tool that writes a file**:
  - iOS: `xcrun simctl io booted screenshot <file>`;
  - Android: `adb exec-out screencap -p > <file>`;
  - Maestro: `takeScreenshot`;
  - web: Playwright (`page.screenshot({ path })`, or `pnpm exec playwright screenshot <url> <file>`).

  The browser and simulator tools' own screenshots are for you to look at; also save a file.
- **Size**: keep each one under about 300 KB. On macOS, `sips -Z 1000 <file>` caps the long side
  at 1000 px.
- **What to capture**: the states the spec asks for, the states named in a criterion marked
  `manual`, and each changed screen. Never capture real personal data or a token.
- **Commit**: leave the files in the working tree. `ship`'s commit step commits them on their own
  as `docs(evidence): screenshots for #<N>`.
- **Missing**: when a shot can't be taken, write down `not captured: <reason>`. Never leave a
  placeholder.

## 7. Clean up

Unless `--keep-running` was passed, stop everything this skill started: `preview_stop` for preview
servers, and stop the background processes and any containers it started. Leave alone what was
already running.

## 8. Report

Show one table: area → what was checked → result → evidence (status codes, console errors, and the
path of each screenshot file under `docs/evidence/<N>/`, or `not captured: <reason>`). Each result is one of:

- **pass**: it behaved as expected.
- **fail**: a real defect. Give the failing case: steps or request, expected, actual.
- **not verified**: it couldn't be run, with the reason. This is not a failure, but never report it
  as a pass.

Save the same table, with the commands and URLs used, to the path printed by
`node ".claude/factory-kit/scripts/report-path.mjs" verify` (run it in the repo; don't build the
path yourself). `describe-pr` reads it from there for the MR's "How tested".

Don't fix defects here unless the user asks; report them.
